chapter_title: Aging: Drugs to Eliminate Methylglyoxal, a Reactive Glucose Metabolite, and Advanced Glycation Endproducts
source_pdf: /mnt/project-files/Experimental Provenance for QSAR Dataset/Pharmacology (Luca Gallelli) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

records.quote: Aminoguanidine potently inhibits histaminases [157, 158] and prevents deamination of histamine and putrescine.
records.notes: Target class (enzyme) is inferred from the name histaminase; the page does not label it an enzyme.

records.mechanism_book_wording: inhibits nitric oxide synthase (NOS) and prevents the formation of nitric oxide (NO)
records.quote: Aminoguanidine also inhibits nitric oxide synthase (NOS) [159, 160] and prevents the formation of nitric oxide (NO)
records.notes: Target class (enzyme) is inferred from the name synthase.

records.role_detail: direction not stated; binds the enzyme
records.mechanism_book_wording: binds to the enzyme S-adenosylmethionine decarboxylase and increases synthesis of polyamines
records.quote: Aminoguanidine also binds to the enzyme S-adenosylmethionine decarboxylase and increases synthesis of polyamines
records.notes: The page says only 'binds to' the enzyme and 'increases synthesis of polyamines'. The role Activator is my inference from the increased polyamine synthesis; the page does not say activator.

records.mechanism_book_wording: a weak inhibitor of thiamine diphosphokinase
records.quote: Alagebrium has been reported to be a weak inhibitor of thiamine diphosphokinase and is unlikely to interfere with thiamine metabolism
records.notes: Drug kind: the book calls it an AGE crosslink breaker studied in phase 2 trials; no formal drug-kind label given.

records.mechanism_book_wording: a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist which acts as an insulin sensitizer
records.quote: Pioglitazone, a thiazolidinedione, is a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist which acts as an insulin sensitizer
records.notes: Drug kind: the book says it is used in type 2 diabetes. The anti-AGE effect (inhibiting AGEs formation) is stated separately and has no named target.

records.quote: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) and angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs) have been shown to protect against kidney damage
records.notes: Class named by target, no compound named. Receptor subtype not stated. The page says the class is proposed to have anti-AGE effects.

records.quote: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) and angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs) have been shown to protect against kidney damage
records.notes: Class named by target, no compound named.

records.quote: These compounds include the cycloxygenase inhibitors, aspirin [186-188], ibuprofen [189], diclofenac [190],
records.notes: Class record only. Aspirin, ibuprofen and diclofenac follow in a list, but the sentence is a list of compounds and it is ambiguous whether each is being called a cyclooxygenase inhibitor, so I did not write separate per-drug records.

records.mechanism_book_wording: increase the activity of several prooxidant enzymes such as NADPH oxidase
records.quote: MG has been shown to increase the activity of several prooxidant enzymes such as NADPH oxidase [94, 97] (Fig. 3)
records.notes: MG is a reactive metabolite, not a drug. Figure 3 (PDF 700) also shows MG acting on NADPH oxidase.

records.mechanism_book_wording: increase the activity of several prooxidant enzymes such as NADPH oxidase ... p38 MAPK
records.quote: MG has been shown to increase the activity of several prooxidant enzymes such as NADPH oxidase [94, 97] (Fig. 3), p38 MAPK [98, 102]
records.notes: p38 MAPK is a kinase (enzyme) by my inference; the page groups it in the list of prooxidant enzymes. The same sentence says MG increases expression of JNK and PPAR-alpha, which I did not record as mechanisms (expression, not a stated activity or ligand effect).

records.mechanism_book_wording: reducing antioxidants such as GSH, glutathione peroxidase, glutathione reductase
records.quote: MG can increase oxidative stress by reducing antioxidants (Fig. 3) such as GSH [104, 106, 107], glutathione peroxidase [108]
records.notes: Page says MG reduces the antioxidant; whether this is activity, level or expression is not stated here. Role Inhibitor is my inference. Figure 3 (PDF 700) shows a down arrow at GSH-Px. PDF 701 reports reduced glutathione peroxidase activity in SHR rats with elevated MG (association).

records.mechanism_book_wording: reducing antioxidants such as GSH, glutathione peroxidase, glutathione reductase
records.quote: glutathione peroxidase [108], glutathione reductase [60, 62, 108, 109], manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) [96]
records.notes: Same sentence as the glutathione peroxidase record; role Inhibitor is my inference (activity vs level not stated). Figure 3 (PDF 700) shows a down arrow at GSH-Red.

records.mechanism_book_wording: reducing antioxidants such as ... manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD)
records.notes: Same sentence as above; role Inhibitor is my inference. Figure 3 shows a down arrow at SOD and at catalase (catalase not recorded separately because it appears only in the figure).

records.role_detail: ligand binding that induces oxidative stress; agonist role inferred
records.mechanism_book_wording: AGEs bind to the receptor for AGEs (RAGE) ... to induce oxidative stress
records.quote: AGEs bind to the receptor for AGEs (RAGE) and scavenger receptors to induce oxidative stress in various cells
records.notes: The page says AGEs bind and induce oxidative stress; it does not use the word agonist. Role Agonist is my inference. Figure 3 (PDF 700) also shows AGEs and RAGE.

records.role_detail: ligand binding that induces oxidative stress; agonist role inferred
records.mechanism_book_wording: AGEs bind to ... scavenger receptors to induce oxidative stress
records.quote: AGEs bind to the receptor for AGEs (RAGE) and scavenger receptors to induce oxidative stress in various cells
records.notes: Scavenger receptor subtype not named. Role Agonist is my inference, as for RAGE.

chapter_notes: Skipped about 4 statements whose targets are neither receptor nor enzyme (phenacylthiazolium bromide and alagebrium breaking AGE cross-links; aminoguanidine, metformin and N-acetylcysteine binding or scavenging MG and dicarbonyls). Many compounds (metformin, NAC, aspirin, vitamins C/E) have only scavenging or chemical effects with no named receptor or enzyme, so are not recorded; the chapter gives no IC50, Ki or similar values for any recorded mechanism (doses appear only in clinical or animal descriptions).
